statedReasoning: Per the fully-fetched bill text and důvodová zpráva (submitted 3 Nov 2025 by Schillerová, Babiš, Okamura, Macinka, Juchelka, Havlíček, Malá, Fiala, Šťastný — ANO/SPD group), the ENTIRE substantive change is one clause: Čl. I replaces, in §14 odst. 5 věta první of zákon č. 589/1992 Sb., the phrase '30 % průměrné mzdy v roce 2024, 35 % průměrné mzdy v roce 2025 a 40 % průměrné mzdy od roku 2026' with '35 % průměrné mzdy' — i.e. it FREEZES the minimum monthly vyměřovací základ (assessment base) for pojistné na důchodové pojištění (pension-insurance premiums) paid by OSVČ (self-employed persons) whose self-employment is their MAIN activity at the 2025 level (35% of average wage), cancelling the scheduled further rise to 40% legislated for 2026 by the 2023 consolidation package (zákon č. 349/2023 Sb., tisk 488 of the 9th electoral term). The DZ explains the 2023 package raised this base in three steps (2024→30%, 2025→35%, 2026→40%) alongside other OSVČ burden increases (minimum annual base 50%→55% of tax base; flat-tax-regime bands raised) enacted 'without adequate assessment of impact on OSVČ's economic situation' amid lingering energy/inflation cost pressure, and proposes freezing only this one parameter as an 'acceptable compromise' rather than reversing the whole package. Transitional provisions (Čl. II) let OSVČ who already paid 2026 advances at the higher (40%) base request a refund of the difference by 31 Dec 2026. Effective the first day of the month after promulgation; the sponsors requested (and per the history, achieved) first-reading passage under §90 odst. 2 of the Chamber's rules of procedure to take effect as fast as possible. Stated fiscal impact: a partial revenue shortfall to the state budget versus the already-legislated 2026 trajectory, which the DZ argues will be offset by higher self-employment activity and reduced grey-economy incentive; no impact on other public budgets; no discriminatory, privacy, corruption-risk, or security impact identified. This affects EVERY main-activity OSVČ nationally, regardless of sector — a universal, individual-level parameter, not a sector- or company-specific measure.
researchedContext:
Legislative history confirms this bill completed the FULL legislative process and is now enacted law: government issued a negative opinion 10 Dec 2025; Organizational Committee referred it 17 Dec 2025 (rapporteur Jiří Havránek, Social Policy Committee as guarantor, per the batch brief also routed to the Budget Committee as a further committee); first reading 16 Jan 2026 rejected the sponsors' expedited-single-reading request and sent it to committees; Budget Committee initially suspended proceedings (23 Jan 2026) before recommending approval (10 Feb 2026); Social Policy Committee endorsed it 19 Feb 2026; second reading 4 Mar 2026 (8 amendments tabled); third reading approved 25 Mar 2026 (vote 80); Senate REJECTED it 6 May 2026; the Chamber overrode the Senate and reaffirmed its original version 26 May 2026; the President signed it 5 June 2026; and it was promulgated as zákon č. 90/2026 Sb. on 10 June 2026 — a contested but fully completed enactment.

SECTOR-ADJACENCY TEST (this batch's special focus for tisk 11): the bill's ONLY changed provision, §14 odst. 5, governs exclusively the OSVČ's OWN minimum individual assessment base for main-activity self-employment. It does NOT touch any employer-side provision of 589/1992 (e.g. the separate employer vyměřovací základ and contribution-rate framework lives in different, untouched sections of the act). The five 'economy'-sector companies flagged as sponsor-adjacent — CHOMUTOVSKÁ BYTOVÁ a.s. (Jan Richter, 104,065,984 CZK), IF Holding a.s. and IF FACILITY a.s. (Radim Fiala, 0 and 11,253,147 CZK), Hartenberg Holding, s.r.o. and IMOBA, a.s. (Andrej Babiš, 0 and 1,823,880 CZK) — are all incorporated companies (a.s./s.r.o.) that, as employers, pay social-security insurance for their own employees on the EMPLOYER side of 589/1992, a mechanism this bill never touches. Independent verification (web) confirms: (1) CHOMUTOVSKÁ BYTOVÁ a.s. is 100%-owned by the Statutární město Chomutov (city of Chomutov) — a municipal housing-management company, not a private real-estate business; notably this batch's own municipalExcludedCompanies list captures the city's separate transport company (Dopravní podnik měst Chomutova a Jirkova a.s.) but NOT Chomutovská bytová, despite identical municipal ownership — a data-quality gap in the exclusion list. (2) IF Holding/IF FACILITY (Fiala) is, per independent investigative reporting (Transparency International, Blesk.cz, Seznam Zprávy), a genuinely private facility-management/security/cleaning group heavily dependent on Prostějov municipal contracts — private, but a services business with no mechanical link to the OSVČ pension-base provision either way. (3) Hartenberg Holding/IMOBA (Babiš) is, per independent reporting (e15.cz, Seznam Zprávy, Czech Wikipedia), a genuinely private real-estate/investment holding (IMOBA owns the Čapí hnízdo estate; Hartenberg finances Prague residential developments) — real, private, and sector-plausible as a business, but again the bill's sole provision has no channel to a company's employer-side insurance costs, since it regulates individual OSVČ status, not corporate payroll.

unstatedEffects.effect: The freeze benefits all main-activity OSVČ nationally by cancelling a scheduled contribution-base increase, at the cost of forgone 2026 state pension-fund revenue versus the already-legislated trajectory (acknowledged only qualitatively in the DZ as a 'partial shortfall', not quantified) — a universal parametric change flowing to a broad occupational class via ČSSZ, with no company or sector named as payee or beneficiary.
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: All main-activity self-employed persons (OSVČ) nationally; the state pension budget forgoes the scheduled 2026 increase.

unstatedEffects.effect: Because the change freezes only the statutory MINIMUM assessment-base floor (not the base for OSVČ who already declare above it), the practical relief is concentrated on lower-earning or marginal self-employed people paying at or near the minimum — a progressive-leaning distributional effect the DZ frames only as 'avoiding a burden increase' for OSVČ generally, without highlighting that higher-earning OSVČ (who already pay above the floor) see no benefit at all.
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: Self-employed persons earning at or near the statutory minimum assessment base; higher-earning OSVČ already above the floor are unaffected.

conflictAssessment: SECTOR-ADJACENCY FINDING (this batch's test case): the 'economy'-sector match is COINCIDENTAL, not a real channel — the same pattern batch-001 found for the raw money signal now recurs for the sector-matched signal. The bill's sole provision regulates an individual OSVČ's own minimum pension-insurance assessment base; it has zero mechanical connection to any company's employer-side social-insurance obligations, so none of the five flagged 'economy' companies — whether municipal (Chomutovská bytová) or genuinely private (IF Holding/IF Facility, Hartenberg/IMOBA) — has a plausible business stake in this specific clause, regardless of how real or substantial those companies' broader business interests are. One nuance flagged honestly rather than strained into a finding: several sponsors (including Fiala, Babiš, and Richter alongside most others in this batch) carry the graph's generic 'OSVČ' tie (company:ico:04627695) at a flat 0 CZK with no distinguishing detail — the same undifferentiated marker recurring across nearly every sponsor in this and the prior batch. Because it carries no individuating financial substance, it cannot support a claim that any specific sponsor personally benefits as an OSVČ from this freeze; it is flagged here as a graph data-quality gap (the marker should differentiate real OSVČ registrations with actual declared income from a boilerplate placeholder) rather than treated as evidence of a conflict. Money ties otherwise recorded for this bill's large sponsor roster (Nacher's Operátor ICT — Prague municipal IT; Šťastný's Pražské služby — Prague municipal waste management, VZP — the public insurer, and Nadační fond Klausových — a charitable foundation; Okamura's MIKI TRAVEL and restaurant/catering ties; Juchelka's public broadcaster and PR-agency ties; Babiš's wider AGROFERT/Synthesia/Kostelecké uzeniny industrial-conglomerate ties) are, as in batch-001's tisk 115 dossier, uniformly unconnected to this bill's narrow OSVČ-insurance-base subject. The honest finding, symmetric across ANO, SPD, and independent sponsors alike, is the absence of a conflict — sector-matching correctly identified sponsors with real private-business ties, but the specific provision those companies were flagged against does not touch their business.

citations.claim: Tisk 11 amends only §14 odst. 5 věta první of zákon č. 589/1992 Sb., freezing the minimum monthly assessment base for main-activity OSVČ's pension-insurance premiums at 35% of average wage (2025 level), cancelling the scheduled rise to 40% legislated for 2026 by the 2023 consolidation package; transitional provisions allow refund requests for 2026 advances already paid at the higher base by 31 Dec 2026. No provision touches employer-side social-insurance obligations. Signed by Schillerová, Babiš, Okamura, Macinka, Juchelka, Havlíček, Malá, Fiala, Šťastný, Prague 3 Nov 2025.

Legislative history: government negative opinion 10 Dec 2025; first reading 16 Jan 2026 (expedited single-reading rejected); Budget Committee suspension then approval; Social Policy Committee endorsement 19 Feb 2026; second reading 4 Mar 2026 (8 amendments); third reading approved 25 Mar 2026 (vote 80); Senate rejected 6 May 2026; Chamber reaffirmed original version 26 May 2026; President signed 5 June 2026; promulgated as zákon č. 90/2026 Sb. on 10 June 2026.
The amended statute is zákon č. 589/1992 Sb., o pojistném na sociální zabezpečení a příspěvku na státní politiku zaměstnanosti — a real, in-force Czech law.

The 2023 consolidation package that established the 2024/2025/2026 escalation this bill partially reverses is zákon č. 349/2023 Sb. — cited within the bill's own amending-law list and its explanatory memorandum; a real Czech law.

CHOMUTOVSKÁ BYTOVÁ a.s. (sponsor Jan Richter's largest tie, 104,065,984 CZK) is 100%-owned by the Statutární město Chomutov — a municipal housing-management company, not a private real-estate business, and structurally analogous to the municipal-board roles this batch already excludes for other companies.

Hartenberg Holding, s.r.o. and IMOBA, a.s. (sponsor Andrej Babiš's ties) are independently confirmed as genuinely private real-estate/investment vehicles, but the bill's sole provision (individual OSVČ assessment base) has no mechanical connection to a company's employer-side insurance obligations.

IF Holding a.s. and IF FACILITY a.s. (sponsor Radim Fiala's ties) are independently confirmed as a private facility-management/security/cleaning group, unrelated in business substance to this bill's OSVČ-insurance-base provision.
Sponsor Boris Šťastný's largest tie, Pražské služby, a.s. (1,470,325,336 CZK), is Prague's municipal waste-management operator, unrelated to this bill's subject.
